claims.text: The Colorado River is 1,450 miles (2,330 km) long, the fifth-longest river in the United States.

The Colorado River and its tributaries are a vital source of water for 40 million people, and an extensive system of dams, reservoirs and aqueducts diverts almost its entire flow for agricultural irrigation and urban water supply.
At Morelos Dam, the entire remaining flow of the Colorado is diverted to irrigate the Mexicali Valley.
Since 1960, the stretch of the Colorado between San Luis Río Colorado and the Gulf of California has been dry or a trickle formed by irrigation return flows.
The Colorado empties into the Gulf of California about 75 miles (120 km) south of Yuma.
After Hoover Dam was built in the 1930s, virtually no freshwater reached the delta for six years while Lake Mead filled behind it.
Before major dams, the delta's wetlands once covered 7,810 km2 (1,930,000 acres).
The loss of freshwater flows to the delta over the twentieth century has reduced delta wetlands to about 5 percent of their original extent.

The first pulse flow, an eight-week release of 105,000 acre-feet starting on March 21, 2014, reached the sea on May 16, 2014, the first time in 16 years that any water from the Colorado flowed into the ocean.
NASA MODIS Terra true-colour pictures of the Colorado River Delta taken on 15 April 2000 and 2024 (NASA GIBS).
